title: Get-Process
description: List running processes as objects, sortable/filterable by any property.
notes: Everything returned is a live .NET object — pipe into Select-Object to pick just the properties you need.

title: Get-Service
description: List Windows services and their current status.
notes: Set-Service can change StartType, e.g. disabling an unnecessary service.

title: Get-EventLog
description: Query classic (pre-Vista style) Windows event logs.
notes: Deprecated in favor of Get-WinEvent, which supports the newer .evtx structured logs and is faster on large logs.

title: Get-WinEvent
description: Query the modern Windows Event Log (including custom/application logs) via structured XML.
notes: FilterHashtable is far faster than piping to Where-Object because filtering happens at the log-provider level.

title: Test-NetConnection
description: Test connectivity to a host/port, replacing ping+telnet for quick checks.
notes: -TraceRoute adds hop-by-hop path info to the same output.

title: Get-ChildItem
description: List items in a container (files/registry/etc). -Force shows hidden items, -Recurse descends subfolders.
notes: 'gci' and 'ls' are built-in aliases for this cmdlet.

title: Copy-Item
description: Copy files, folders, or other provider items (registry, cert store).
notes: Works across PS providers, e.g. copying a registry key: Copy-Item HKLM:\...\Run HKCU:\...\Run.

title: Move-Item
description: Move or rename files, folders, or other provider items.
notes: Combine with -WhatIf to preview the operation before executing it for real.

title: Remove-Item
description: Delete files, folders, or other provider items.
notes: -WhatIf shows what would be deleted without actually deleting — always test destructive scripts this way first.

title: New-Item
description: Create a new file, directory, symlink, or other provider item.
notes: -ItemType SymbolicLink creates a symlink (requires elevated privileges or Developer Mode).

title: Get-ADUser
description: Query Active Directory user objects (requires the RSAT ActiveDirectory module).
notes: -Properties * pulls every AD attribute, but is slower — only request what you need in large domains.

title: Invoke-WebRequest
description: Send an HTTP/HTTPS request and return the response object (headers, content, status).
notes: Invoke-RestMethod is the sibling cmdlet that auto-parses JSON/XML responses instead of returning raw HTML.

title: Get-LocalUser
description: List local user accounts (modern replacement for 'net user').
notes: Pairs with Get-LocalGroupMember to audit local Administrators group membership.

title: Get-LocalGroupMember
description: List members of a local group.
notes: Unexpected members here are a very common privilege-escalation / persistence finding.

title: Set-ExecutionPolicy
description: Configure the script-execution restriction level for the current session/machine.
notes: Execution policy is a safety rail, not a security boundary — it can be bypassed with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass by design.

title: Get-Content
description: Read the contents of a file (Windows equivalent of cat/tail).
notes: -Wait behaves like 'tail -f', streaming new lines as they are appended.

title: Select-String
description: Search text/files for a regex pattern (PowerShell's grep).
notes: -Context 2,2 shows two lines of context before/after each match.

title: Get-Item / Set-ItemProperty
description: Read or write registry values through the Registry PS provider.
notes: HKLM: and HKCU: are pre-mounted PSDrives, so you navigate the registry like a filesystem.

title: Get-NetTCPConnection
description: List active TCP connections as objects, with the owning process ID.
notes: Pipe OwningProcess into Get-Process -Id to resolve it to a process name in one line.

title: Get-FileHash
description: Compute a cryptographic hash of a file — the built-in PowerShell equivalent of sha256sum.
notes: Default algorithm is SHA256; MD5/SHA1 are also supported but weaker.

title: Get-ScheduledTask
description: List scheduled tasks as objects, replacing schtasks for scripting scenarios.
notes: Get-ScheduledTaskInfo adds LastRunTime/NextRunTime — useful for spotting stealthy persistence tasks.

title: Get-Acl / Set-Acl
description: View or set NTFS/registry access control lists as objects.
notes: Set-Acl requires an ACL object, typically built by editing the output of Get-Acl and piping it back.

title: ConvertTo-Json / ConvertFrom-Json
description: Serialize PowerShell objects to/from JSON, useful for logging and API interop.
notes: -Depth controls how deeply nested objects are serialized; the default (2) truncates complex objects silently.

title: Export-Csv / Import-Csv
description: Write/read objects to/from CSV, a common way to hand data off to spreadsheets.
notes: -NoTypeInformation removes the '#TYPE' header line that Excel otherwise chokes on.

title: Invoke-Command
description: Run a script block on one or more remote computers via WinRM (PS Remoting).
notes: Requires PS Remoting enabled (Enable-PSRemoting) and appropriate WinRM firewall rules on the target.

title: Get-Hotfix
description: List installed Windows updates/hotfixes.
notes: Cross-reference HotFixID values against a CVE's KB number during patch-compliance checks.

title: Get-WmiObject / Get-CimInstance
description: Query WMI/CIM classes for system, hardware and OS information (CimInstance is the modern, faster cmdlet).
notes: Win32_Process includes ParentProcessId, letting you reconstruct a process tree without extra tools.

title: Start-Process / Stop-Process
description: Launch or terminate processes from PowerShell.
notes: -Verb RunAs launches the process elevated, triggering a UAC prompt.

title: Get-Random
description: Generate a pseudo-random number or pick a random item from a collection.
notes: Not cryptographically secure — use [System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator] for that.

title: Where-Object / ForEach-Object
description: Filter (Where-Object) and iterate (ForEach-Object) over pipeline objects — the workhorses of PS scripting.
notes: $_ refers to the current pipeline object inside the script block.

title: Compare-Object
description: Compare two collections and show the differences between them.
notes: '=>' marks items only in the second set, '<=' only in the first — handy for diffing config baselines.

title: Get-Credential
description: Prompt the user securely for a username/password, returning a PSCredential object.
notes: Never hardcode plaintext passwords in scripts — use Get-Credential or a secrets vault instead.

title: New-PSSession / Enter-PSSession
description: Open an interactive remote PowerShell session over WinRM.
notes: Exit-PSSession or 'exit' returns you to the local session.

title: Get-Module / Import-Module
description: List loaded or installable PowerShell modules; Import-Module loads one into the session.
notes: 'Get-Module -ListAvailable' shows every module installed on disk, not just currently loaded ones.

title: Set-MpPreference / Get-MpThreatDetection
description: Query or configure Windows Defender (the built-in antimalware engine).
notes: Get-MpComputerStatus shows whether real-time protection and signature updates are current.

title: Get-DnsClientCache
description: View the local DNS resolver cache as objects (modern replacement for 'ipconfig /displaydns').
notes: Clear-DnsClientCache is the object-cmdlet equivalent of 'ipconfig /flushdns'.

title: Get-Clipboard / Set-Clipboard
description: Read or write the Windows clipboard contents from a script.
notes: Attackers occasionally harvest clipboard contents — this cmdlet is the built-in, no-download way to inspect it during triage.

title: Test-Path
description: Check whether a file, folder, or registry path exists, returning $true/$false.
notes: Works across every PS provider (filesystem, registry, cert store), not just the filesystem.
